Alex / Marissa — notes below (technical):

1) Tenant isolation:
- Dedicated pools: Redwood Dedicated supports single-tenant GPU pools per customer. Isolation is enforced at the orchestration and network layer — dedicated VPCs, strict IAM role separation, per-tenant key encryption keys (KMS), and no shared host network namespaces for tenant workloads.
- For hosted (shared) offerings we use per-tenant logical isolation via namespaces, strict RBAC, and KV cache partitioning; sensitive workloads can be moved to Dedicated or Private.

2) Metering & billing:
- Marketplace integrations: We support partner-side metering APIs for AWS and usage-based metering via partner metering mechanisms. For Azure/GCP we integrate via partner billing connectors where available; consolidated billing through the marketplace (customer invoices through marketplace) is supported where the marketplace provides that flow.
- For customers who purchase directly, we also support usage export to customer billing systems (CSV/S3) for reconciliation.

3) Data handling & retention:
- Hosted default: ephemeral KV caches are scoped per-request and flushed after session TTL (default 24h) unless customers opt into persistent caching. Analytics pipelines only collect aggregated telemetry; no raw customer prompt/response data is stored in analytics unless explicitly enabled for debugging (this requires opt-in).
- Private/Dedicated: option to disable telemetry forwarding and set retention to zero days.

4) Compliance artifacts:
- We can provide a SOC 2 Type II snapshot (most recently audited May 2028) and an encryption whitepaper.

5) Marketplace listing path:
- We support both private and public listings. Typical timeline: private listing: ~2-3 weeks (contract + entity docs + technical verification). Public listing: ~4-8 weeks (marketplace review, security checks, and pricing/terms negotiation).

I'll attach the architecture summary and a short metering flow diagram for Alex to send.

-Karthik

Hi Sofia — thanks for the checklist. Below are consolidated answers tied to the five questions you sent; I attached the SOC2 snapshot and architecture summary for your security team to review. If you want a short walkthrough call early next week we can run the procurement and security teams through the diagrams.

1) Tenant isolation:
- Dedicated listings: Redwood Dedicated supports single-tenant deployments (per-customer GPU pools) with dedicated VPCs, per-tenant KMS keys, and orchestration-level isolation. No tenant workloads share host network namespaces. This is our recommended path when strict isolation is required.
- Hosted (standard): logical isolation via namespaces, RBAC, and per-tenant KV cache partitions. For workloads needing stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

2) Metering & billing:
- Redwood supports partner-side metering for AWS marketplace and equivalent partner metering connectors for Azure and GCP where marketplaces provide the capability. We can publish metering reports to the marketplace metering API in near-real time. Consolidated billing through the marketplace is supported where the marketplace operator exposes that option; otherwise we provide usage exports for reconciliation.

3) Data handling & retention:
- Default (hosted): ephemeral KV caches cleared after session TTL (default 24 hours). Analytics capture aggregated telemetry only; we do not persist raw prompt/response pairs in analytics without explicit customer opt-in.
- Options: Private/Dedicated deployments allow disabling telemetry forwarding and setting retention to customer-specified values (including zero).

4) Compliance artifacts:
- Attached: soc2-snapshot-2028-05.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary) and redwood-marketplace-architecture-summary.pdf (encryption and network controls). We encrypt in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256) with per-tenant KMS integration available for Dedicated and Private deployments.

5) Marketplace listing path & timeline:
- Private listing: collect entity declaration + addendum (we provide templates) + technical verification — typical timeline 2-3 weeks.
- Public listing: includes marketplace security review and pricing/terms negotiation — typical timeline 4-8 weeks depending on queue and certification steps.

Attachments included: redwood-marketplace-architecture-summary.pdf, soc2-snapshot-2028-05.pdf, seller-entity-declaration.docx
